skills.name: How Germany established its Cameroon claim

note.text: German firms helped prepare coastal agreements and encouraged imperial action. Gustav Nachtigal acted as the imperial commissioner. The German-Duala treaty conventionally dated 12 July 1884 preceded the flag ceremony on 14 July. British Consul Edward Hewett arrived after the German claim. Timing, commercial preparation and diplomatic action mattered, but a coastal assertion was not immediate control of all Cameroon. Later expansion involved further agreements and violence, and local opposition continued.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Compare the functions of a trader, a coastal signatory and an imperial commissioner. They are not interchangeable. A timeline should distinguish the treaty date from the flag date and then leave room for the later spread of rule. The Berlin Conference began later that year and did not itself sign the coastal treaty.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Use dates to test causal statements: an event occurring later cannot be the earlier event's signing. Ask what a document claims and whose authority it represents. The formula Germany succeeded should describe the establishment of an imperial claim, not imply that colonial coercion was morally justified.
